prerequisites: Knowledges of phisics, thermodynamic and energy systems

learning_outcomes.text: Students will acquire an in-depth understanding of the theoretical and scientific principles governing complex energy systems, including the thermodynamic, thermo-fluid dynamic, thermo-chemical and electrical phenomena that determine the operation of industrial plants.

The course introduces advanced methods and tools for modelling, simulating and designing energy components and systems, together with criteria for analysing industrial processes and assessing their energy and environmental performance.

Students will also develop a systemic understanding of the energy transition, including its regulatory, technological and methodological implications, as well as the methods needed to conceive, plan and manage complex and innovative systems and services.
Moreover, the course provides methodological bases for performing experimental activities and energy diagnostics in articulated industrial contexts.

Upon completing the course, students will be able to apply the acquired knowledge to model and interpret the behaviour of complex energy systems and to analyse components and plants using thermo-economic modelling, numerical simulation and performance evaluation tools.
They will be able to conduct experiments and use advanced instrumentation for energy monitoring, critically evaluating results and associated uncertainties.
Students will also be capable of designing, planning and managing energy conversion systems and complex industrial plants, integrating technical, economic and environmental considerations.
They will learn to address typical industrial and energy engineering problems by identifying constraints, solutions and improvement opportunities.
The course also enables students to assess the integration of renewable technologies and innovative energy systems with a view to sustainability and competitiveness.
And to evaluate processes, technologies and plants considering their economic and managerial implications.
The competencies acquired provide a solid foundation for further advanced studies or research activities.
Students will develop the ability to independently analyse data, indicators and information from industrial plants and processes, formulating objective and coherent assessments.
They will be able to compare alternative technical solutions and make informed decisions based on technical standards, design constraints and principles of efficiency and sustainability.

The course supports the development of autonomy in organising activities, managing time and resources, and planning energy improvement interventions, as well as fostering awareness of the need for continuous professional development.

The course strengthens the student’s ability to communicate energy-related issues, analyses and solutions clearly and effectively to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, developing skills in drafting technical energy management reports and presenting energy scenarios.

Particular attention is given to the use of graphs, diagrams, indicators and quantitative representations to illustrate performance and interventions, together with awareness of the ethical, environmental and economic implications of engineering decisions.

Finally, the course enhances the student’s ability to independently update their knowledge of technological, regulatory and methodological developments in the energy sector, to perform bibliographic and technical research using major scientific databases, and to learn through real-world problems and project-based activities, in line with the Problem-Based Learning approach.

syllabus_topics: Overview of the main energy generation technologies
Load curve of the national electric grid
NPV (Net Present Value), IRR (Internal Rate of Return), DPBT (Discounted Payback Time), and other economic indicators
Relationship between NPV and plant profitability
Pumps: Characteristic curves as a function of rotational speed
Pumps: Example calculation of pump operating point
Pumps: Pumps in series and parallel
Fire-tube boilers: Thermodynamic analysis of fire-tube boilers
Fire-tube boilers: Safety issues related to fire-tube boilers
Thermal insulation: Heat transfer equations for conduction and convection
Thermal insulation: Heat transfer equations for pipes (cylindrical systems)
Thermal insulation: Critical insulation radius for pipes
Thermal insulation: Economic insulation thickness and related trends
Relationship between energy consumption and production
Energy performance indicators and universal diagram
LNG supply chain: liquefaction and regasification systems
Analysis of energy flows in major industrial sectors: glass industry, paper industry, textile industry, and tanning industry
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on the oral examination (main component), the technical report (for 9-ECTS students), and attendance and participation in seminars/visits. A satisfactory technical report is required for 9-ECTS students to sit the oral examination. Unjustified absences from seminars negatively affect the final mark. The final mark reflects theoretical knowledge, applied skills, communication abilities, and autonomous judgment.
